page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. This configuration provides 16 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) across 8 physical cores, utilizing 2 threads per core. The processor is equipped with 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier status in Geekbench single-core (2211.0) and text processing (2952.0) tests, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Single-threaded compression and decompression are also strong, with gzip compression reaching 34.45 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.45 GB/sec. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall within the average range, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 17296.91 and uncached read memory bandwidth at 121.51 GB/sec. For small LLM inference using a 135M model, text generation is highly efficient at 348.03 tokens/sec, while larger 7B model processing remains average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.4xlarge offers a balanced resource density for compute-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enhances its value for specialized vector and matrix mathematics without the overhead of dedicated accelerator hardware. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as single-threaded data processing, text manipulation, software compilation, lightweight machine learning inference, and general compute-intensive applications.
